newsitem.title: USA: Clinton 20 points ahead in California -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Clinton 20 points ahead in California -- poll.

text.p: President Clinton holds a 20 percentage point lead over Republican Bob Dole in California, according to a new poll published Wednesday that will come as another blow to the Dole campaign.

Clinton led Dole among likely voters by 54 to 34 percent in the Los Angeles Times poll taken Oct. 17-21. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot scored 6 percent and Green Party candidate Ralph Nader 3 percent. The margin of error was plus or minus three percentage points.

Dole decided last week to concentrate many of his remaining resources on California after a poll by another organisation said he had cut Clinton's lead in the state to 10 points. He is spending heavily on television advertisements in California, which has some of the most expensive media markets in the country, and has dispatched many campaign operatives to the state in a last-ditch effort to turn the election around.
California, the most populous state, has 54 electoral votes -- one fifth of the 270 in the Electoral College needed to win the presidency.

In an analysis of the survey, the Times said Clinton led even in sub-groups where Dole should have been strong. The president led among white males by 45 to 36 percent, among moderate voters by 63 to 22 percent and among independents by 46 to 23 percent. Asked who they would vote for in their congressional districts, 50 percent said Democrats while 44 percent said Republicans.
